principles.critique_request: Show where the response judges a person's whole character by their virtues alone while ignoring that a single particular fault takes corruption from the general censure, contradicting Hamlet's argument.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it acknowledges that a single vicious mole of nature or habit can soil a man's reputation and take corruption from his otherwise pure virtues.

principles.source_thesis: The Ghost commands revenge for foul and unnatural murder, yet charges that in pursuing it Hamlet taint not his mind nor contrive anything against his mother, leaving her to heaven.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response either counsels passivity toward the murder or extends vengeance against the mother, contradicting the Ghost's command to revenge the murder while leaving Gertrude to heaven.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it pursues revenge for the father's murder as a bound duty while keeping the mind untainted and leaving the mother to heaven and the thorns in her bosom.

principles.source_thesis: Foul deeds will rise, though all the earth o'erwhelm them, to men's eyes; hidden wrongdoing cannot stay buried.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response assumes wrongdoing can remain permanently concealed, contradicting Hamlet's claim that foul deeds will rise to men's eyes however they are buried.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response to affirm that concealed foul deeds will inevitably come to light, since nothing can o'erwhelm them from men's eyes forever.

principles.source_thesis: There are more things in heaven and earth than are dreamt of in one's philosophy; the strange should be welcomed as a stranger rather than dismissed.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response dismisses what exceeds its philosophy as fantasy, contradicting Hamlet's charge that there are more things in heaven and earth than are dreamt of in Horatio's philosophy.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it treats the strange and wondrous as a stranger to be welcomed, acknowledging that heaven and earth hold more than any philosophy dreams of.

principles.source_thesis: The time is out of joint, and one may be cursed to be born to set it right.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response treats the disorder of the times as someone else's concern or as easily ignored, contradicting the claim that the time is out of joint and one is born to set it right.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it accepts the burden of a disjointed time and the cursed duty of being born to set it right.

principles.source_thesis: By indirections find directions out: one may use a bait of falsehood to take the carp of truth in order to discover another's conduct.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response rejects all indirect inquiry as dishonest, ignoring Polonius's argument that by windlasses and assays of bias one may find directions out.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response to employ indirect inquiry—laying slight sullies and observing how a party closes with them—as a warranted way to discover the truth of another's behavior.

principles.source_thesis: Love's violent property fordoes itself and leads the will to desperate undertakings, as any passion that afflicts our natures.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats love as always steady and self-governing, contradicting Polonius's claim that love's violent property fordoes itself and drives the will to desperate undertakings.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it recognizes that violent love can undo itself and drive a person to desperate undertakings, as other afflicting passions do.

principles.source_thesis: To be honest, as this world goes, is to be one man picked out of ten thousand.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response assumes honesty is common and easy in the world, contradicting Hamlet's claim that an honest man is one picked out of ten thousand.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it reflects that true honesty is exceedingly rare, one man chosen from ten thousand, rather than the ordinary condition of people.

principles.source_thesis: There is nothing either good or bad but thinking makes it so; Denmark is a prison only to him who thinks it so.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response treats circumstances as inherently good or bad independent of the mind's framing, contradicting Hamlet's claim that thinking makes a thing so.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it holds that a place or condition is a prison only to the mind that thinks it so, since nothing is good or bad but thinking makes it so.

principles.source_thesis: A man may smile and smile and be a villain; outward courtesy cannot be trusted as proof of inward honesty.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats smiling courtesy as reliable evidence of goodwill, contradicting Hamlet's note that one may smile and smile and be a villain.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it distrusts outward smiles and courtesy, remembering that a smiling villain is possible, at least in Denmark.

principles.source_thesis: The readiness is all; since no man knows aught of what he leaves, what is it to leave betimes?
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats timing of death as something to be anxiously calculated, contradicting the claim that the readiness is all and that leaving betimes matters little since no man knows what he leaves.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it rests on readiness rather than anxious calculation, affirming that since no man knows aught of what he leaves, it is little to leave betimes.

principles.source_thesis: Use every man after his desert, and who should 'scape whipping? Treat sinners according to their own instruction, and their own sins will teach them.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response demands strict desert-based punishment of all, ignoring Hamlet's point that using every man after his desert would leave none unwhipped.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it tempers judgment with the recognition that using every man after his desert would leave no one unwhipped, and lets a sinner's own sins instruct him.

principles.source_thesis: The play's purpose is to hold the mirror up to nature, to show virtue her own feature and scorn her own image, so the guilty are struck to the soul.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response treats drama as mere entertainment or flattery, contradicting the argument that playing should hold the mirror up to nature and show virtue and scorn their own features.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it treats the play as a mirror held up to nature, showing virtue her feature and scorn her image so that guilt is struck to the soul.

principles.source_thesis: One may put an antic disposition on—an assumed strangeness—while keeping one's true understanding hidden from observers.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats Hamlet's strange behavior as pure madness without design, ignoring his declared intent to put an antic disposition on.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it accounts for an assumed antic disposition worn deliberately, with true understanding kept hidden behind it.

principles.source_thesis: A man's o'ergrowth of some complexion or habit that too much o'erleavens the form of plausible manners can break down the pales and forts of reason.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats habit as harmless and unrelated to reason, contradicting the argument that an overgrown complexion or habit can break down the pales and forts of reason.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it warns that a habit too much o'erleavening one's manners can break down the pales and forts of reason.

principles.source_thesis: The funeral baked meats did coldly furnish forth the marriage tables: hasty remarriage after a spouse's death is a wicked speed that cannot come to good.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats a swift remarriage after death as natural and harmless, contradicting Hamlet's charge of wicked speed and his certainty that it cannot come to good.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it condemns the indecent haste of remarrying so soon that the funeral meats furnish the wedding tables, and holds that such speed cannot come to good.

principles.source_thesis: Frailty, thy name is woman: a person may hang on a spouse as if appetite grew by what it fed on, yet within a month follow the body and then marry another.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response treats inconstancy in love as impossible or foreign to human nature, contradicting the text's charge of frailty and the swift turn from mourning to remarriage.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it acknowledges human frailty in love, where seeming devotion can give way within a month to a new marriage.

principles.source_thesis: A brother may warn a sister against a suitor's trifling favor, yet must not himself tread the primrose path of dalliance while showing her the steep and thorny way to heaven.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response lets a counselor preach restraint while excusing his own indulgence, contradicting Ophelia's charge against ungracious pastors who show the thorny way while treading the primrose path.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the one who gives the good lesson keeps it as watchman to his own heart and does not tread the primrose path of dalliance himself.

principles.source_thesis: Do not slander any moment of leisure by giving words or talk to a forbidden suitor; a daughter should obey her father's charge to repel his letters and deny his access.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response encourages continuing secret communication with a suitor against a parent's charge, contradicting the command to repel letters and deny access.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it obeys the charge to be scanter of maiden presence and to give no words or talk to the forbidden lord.

principles.source_thesis: Neither a borrower nor a lender be, for loan oft loses both itself and friend, and borrowing dulls the edge of husbandry.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response recommends lending freely or borrowing as prudent, contradicting the precept that loan loses both itself and friend and borrowing dulls husbandry.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response to advise neither borrowing nor lending, since loans lose both money and friends and borrowing blunts thrift.

principles.source_thesis: Costly thy habit as thy purse can buy, but not expressed in fancy; rich, not gaudy, for the apparel oft proclaims the man.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response treats dress as irrelevant or as an occasion for gaudy display, contradicting the precept to dress richly but not gaudily, as one's purse allows.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it advises apparel as costly as one's purse permits but free of fancy—rich, not gaudy—since apparel oft proclaims the man.

principles.source_thesis: Beware of entrance to a quarrel, but being in, bear it that the opposed may beware of thee.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response either invites quarrels carelessly or counsels yielding weakly once engaged, contradicting the precept to avoid quarrels but, once in, to bear oneself so the opponent isware.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response to avoid entering quarrels, yet once engaged to bear the quarrel so that the opposed party may beware.

principles.source_thesis: Those friends whose adoption is tried should be grappled to the soul with hoops of steel, but one should not dull the palm with every new-hatched, unfledged comrade.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats all new acquaintances as equal to tested friends, contradicting the precept to clasp tried friends with hoops of steel while not welcoming every new-hatched comrade.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it grapples tried and adopted friends to the soul with hoops of steel while withholding easy welcome from untested new comrades.

principles.source_thesis: Give every man thine ear but few thy voice; take each man's censure but reserve thy judgement.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response urges speaking one's judgment to everyone while listening to few, contradicting the precept to give every man thine ear but few thy voice.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response to listen to every man, speak to few, take each man's censure, and reserve judgement.

principles.source_thesis: The readiness is all; a man should not fear death, since the soul is immortal and no harm can reach it.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response counsels fear of death as the ultimate harm, contradicting Hamlet's claim that he sets his life at a pin's fee and the soul is immortal as the spirit itself.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it sets life at a pin's fee and trusts that no harm can come to the immortal soul, resting on readiness rather than fear.

principles.source_thesis: Heaven will direct it; one should follow where fate cries out even when friends counsel restraint.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats fate as something to be resisted by friends' counsel, contradicting the claim that heaven will direct the issue and that fate cries out to be followed.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it follows the call of fate while trusting that heaven will direct the outcome, even when others urge restraint.

principles.source_thesis: Something is rotten in the state of Denmark; a portentous apparition bodes some strange eruption to the state.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats the state's disorder as trivial or unrelated to the supernatural portents, contradicting the claim that something is rotten in the state and the apparition bodes eruption.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it recognizes that the armed apparition and the nightly watch bode some strange eruption to the state, and that something is rotten in Denmark.

principles.source_thesis: The spirit is dumb to some and will speak only to the one it seeks; what is seen must be imparted to the person most concerned.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response withholds a grave sight from the person most concerned, contradicting the judgment that the spirit, dumb to the watchers, will speak to Hamlet and that duty requires acquainting him.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it imparts the troubling sight to the person most concerned, as needful in love and fitting duty, trusting the spirit will speak to him.

principles.source_thesis: Virtue itself 'scapes not calumnious strokes; the canker galls the infants of spring too oft before their buttons be disclosed.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response assumes that virtue alone protects one from slander, contradicting the warning that virtue itself escapes not calumnious strokes.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it warns that even virtue is not safe from calumny, as the canker galls spring's infants before their buds open.

principles.source_thesis: Youth to itself rebels, though none else be near; therefore be wary, for best safety lies in fear.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats youth as naturally self-governing and safe without vigilance, contradicting the claim that youth rebels against itself even when none else is near.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it counsels wariness on the ground that youth rebels against itself even in solitude, and best safety lies in fear.

principles.source_thesis: A daughter's duty and obedience require showing a father her suitor's letters and giving his solicitations to his ear.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response counsels a daughter to conceal a suitor's letters from her father, contradicting the text's pattern of obedience in showing the letters and reporting his solicitations.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the daughter, in duty and obedience, shows the suitor's letters and reports his solicitations to her father's ear.

principles.source_thesis: A father may set his daughter as bait to test a suitor's love, observing the encounter from behind an arras to learn whether the love is real.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response refuses all observation or testing of a suitor's love, contradicting the plan to loose the daughter to him and mark the encounter from behind the arras.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it tests the suitor's love by observing an arranged encounter, judging whether he loves her or is fallen from reason thereon.

principles.source_thesis: Madness may hit on pregnant replies that reason and sanity could not so prosperously deliver; there may be method in apparent madness.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response dismisses all strange speech as meaningless, contradicting the observation that though this be madness, yet there is method in it and madness hits on pregnant replies.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it recognizes that apparent madness may carry method and hit on pregnant replies that sanity could not deliver.

principles.source_thesis: A prince is out of a subject's star; unequal rank makes a match unfit, and a father must forbid it.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats rank as irrelevant to the fitness of a match, contradicting the judgment that Lord Hamlet is a prince out of Ophelia's star and this must not be.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it acknowledges that unequal rank makes the match unfit—he is a prince, out of her star, and this must not be.

principles.source_thesis: One may not take from another anything one would more willingly part with than one's life; tedious old fools are to be parted from gladly.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats the parting from a tedious counselor as a loss to be mourned, contradicting Hamlet's wish to part with nothing more willingly except his life.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it parts gladly from tedious company, taking from the counselor nothing it would more willingly give up except life itself.

principles.source_thesis: Denmark's a prison, and there is nothing either good or bad but thinking makes it so; to one mind it is a prison, to another none.
principles.critique_request: Show where the response treats a place as objectively a prison for everyone, contradicting the claim that it is a prison only to the mind that thinks it so.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it holds that a place is a prison to the mind that deems it so, while to another mind it is none, since thinking makes it so.

principles.source_thesis: One should be even and direct with friends, and a friend's free visitation should be distinguished from a sending-for by the King and Queen.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats a summoned visit as a free act of friendship, contradicting the demand to deal justly and confess whether one was sent for.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it deals justly and directly, confessing when a visit was commanded rather than freely chosen, by the rights of fellowship and the consonancy of youth.

principles.source_thesis: The world's grown honest is news that would mean doomsday is near; such news is not true.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats the world as having grown honest, contradicting the exchange in which such news is declared untrue and doomsday near.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it doubts that the world has grown honest, treating such a report as untrue and a sign that doomsday is near.

principles.source_thesis: A king may go a progress through the guts of a beggar; death levels all, and the dust of a great man may stop a bung-hole.

principles.source_thesis: Custom more honoured in the breach than the observance: a drunken national custom soils the name of a whole people and takes from their achievements the pith and marrow of their attribute.

principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it condemns the drunken revel as a custom more honoured in the breach, one that makes the nation traduced and soils its addition.

principles.source_thesis: A brother's hand can dispatch a sleeping man of life, crown, and queen at once, cutting him off in the blossoms of his sin, unhouseled and unaneled.

principles.source_thesis: Lust, though linked to a radiant angel, will sate itself in a celestial bed and prey on garbage; virtue is never moved though lewdness court it in a shape of heaven.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response treats lust as capable of true constancy or virtue as easily seduced, contradicting the claim that virtue will never be moved and lust will prey on garbage.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it holds that virtue is never moved though lewdness courts it in heavenly shape, while lust will sate itself and prey on garbage.

principles.source_thesis: A son is bound to revenge a father's foul murder when he hears it, and should sweep to it as swiftly as meditation or thoughts of love.

principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so the son, hearing of the foul murder, sweeps to revenge as swiftly as meditation or the thoughts of love.

principles.source_thesis: One may wipe from the table of memory all trivial fond records and let a single commandment live alone within the book of the brain, unmixed with baser matter.
principles.critique_request: Identify how the response lets trivial memories and distractions dilute a solemn charge, contradicting the resolve to wipe away all trivial fond records and keep the commandment alone in the brain.
principles.revision_request: Rewrite the response so it wipes away all trivial fond records and lets the solemn charge live alone within the book and volume of the brain, unmixed with baser matter.

principles.source_thesis: The funeral baked meats did coldly furnish forth the marriage tables; a wedding following hard upon a funeral is a sign of thrift misapplied and indecent speed.
principles.critique_request: Point out where the response treats a wedding following immediately on a funeral as fitting and generous, contradicting the charge of wicked speed and coldly furnished tables.
